title: Economics, Not Summits
paragraphs: The hosts of the COP31 summit, Turkey and Australia, are urging a clean energy revolution while expanding fossil fuel production: Turkey has announced two new oilfields and a plan to double natural gas output, and Australia has approved projects that include a coal mine extension that critics call a climate bomb. Collective climate action has effectively stalled since the 2015 Paris Agreement, which nevertheless shaved more than 1C off the projected warming trajectory, and current policies still point towards a rise of about 2.7C by 2100, according to Climate Action Tracker. There is one encouraging sign: the Global Carbon Budget expects fossil fuel emissions to fall slightly in 2026, by 0.4 per cent, although that drop would not have occurred without the oil price spike caused by the Iran war.

The central argument is that economics, rather than diplomacy, is now driving the transition. Solar generates ten times more energy than when the Paris deal was signed, making it the fastest-growing source of electricity ever, and electricity from solar and wind costs less on average than electricity from gas or coal. Auke Hoekstra of Eindhoven University of Technology contends that policy was never the main driver, because the technologies are simply superior; Texas, the leading oil-producing state, has become the leading producer of solar and wind power, and in Nigeria and Pakistan households are installing cheap Chinese panels instead of waiting for governments to upgrade unreliable fossil-fuelled grids. Cheap batteries are solving the remaining drawback, that solar and wind produce little energy during evening peak demand.

Policy still matters, however, since early subsidies and regulations in China and Germany created the conditions for renewables to fall down the cost curve, and governments continue to provide more than 900 billion dollars a year in support for fossil fuels. Expanding the grid is the biggest bottleneck, something governments could speed up by cutting red tape and offering subsidies and loans. Kingsmill Bond of the think tank Ember Energy believes that the economics of clean technology will allow the world to limit warming to well below 2.7C, with the exact outcome depending on politics, and he proposes that energy-importing countries convene their own COP in which fossil fuel exporters cannot delay progress.

options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: Nijerya ve Pakistan'da haneler ucuz panelleri hükümetleri beklemeden kurar.

options.text: The expansion of solar and wind in Texas suggests that fossil fuels and renewables can grow side by side.
options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: önde gelen petrol üreticisi eyalet aynı zamanda önde gelen güneş ve rüzgâr üreticisidir.

options.text: Cheap batteries address a remaining weakness of solar and wind, namely their low output during evening peak demand.
options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: ucuz bataryalar akşam talep zirvesindeki düşük üretimi çözer.

questions.prompt: What does Bond's proposal most strongly imply about the current climate negotiations?

options.text: They are dominated by importing countries that have little to lose from a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
options.explanation: Bond'un önerisi tersini ima eder: ilerlemeyi geciktirebilenler fosil yakıt ihracatçılarıdır.

options.text: They have already delivered the policies needed to keep warming well below 2.7C by the end of the century.
options.explanation: Bond'un beklentisi ekonomiye dayanır; mevcut politikalar yaklaşık 2,7C artışa işaret eder.

options.text: They allow countries that export fossil fuels to slow progress, in a way that the proposed new forum would prevent.
options.explanation: Bond ihracatçıların ilerlemeyi geciktiremeyeceği ayrı bir COP önerir; bu, mevcut müzakerelerde bunun yapılabildiğini ima eder.

options.text: They have no bearing on the transition, since market forces alone determine how quickly it proceeds.
options.explanation: Bond sonucun siyasete bağlı olacağını söyler ve yeni bir müzakere forumu önerir; müzakereleri etkisiz saysaydı bunu önermezdi.
